newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends down but off lows after JGB dip.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends down but off lows after JGB dip.

text.p: The benchmark three-month December euroyen futures contract ended down but off earlier lows in thin Wednesday trade, after coming under pressure on heavy sales of Japanese government bonds (JGBs), traders said.
There also appeared to be some speculative selling in an attempt to test the downside near 99.05 yen, but this failed.
Key December settled at 99.09, down from 99.13 on Tuesday, with turnover of 31,988 contracts.
"Volume was thin in comparison to how much it moved today, and this of course exaggerated moves as well," one trader with a securities firm said.

JGBs tumbled in the afternoon after the contract confirmed resistance at around 124.30, with sentiment also hurt by falls in bank debentures after a domestic newspaper report, later denied, said the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau had not bought bank debentures since April.
But the key September 10-year JGB futures contract managed to pick itself up from a low of 123.80 to end at 123.99, down 0.31 from Tuesday's close.

This slide below 124 yen pushed the key December euroyen contract below an old technical point of 99.08 to an eventual low of 99.07, traders said. But they added that much of the selling appeared to be limited to book-squaring.
"We've seen some fairly steady rises over the past few days, so the market was about due for some downward adjustment," one city bank trader said.

Some speculative sales were triggered as operators tested the downside near 99.05, but this held steady, another city bank trader said. "Trade has been very thin between 99.05 to 99.09, leaving the market vulnerable to some falls," he added.
